My dog ​​is a patient of Dr. Trubert, and every time she goes, she's absolutely delighted to see her. I'm used to seeing trembling, stressed animals in the vet's waiting room, but I have to admit, here it's quite the opposite.

Beyond that, I really appreciate her approach, her professionalism, and the fact that she doesn't push unnecessary treatments. I recommend her without hesitation.

My two cats, Elio and Naïa, have been going to the Sevetys clinic for almost a year now. I've had the opportunity to see Dr. Trubert several times and Dr. Beunier once, both excellent professionals who are incredibly gentle with animals. Elio and Naïa are seen by Dr. Trubert, who takes the time to explain each procedure, the minor health problems cats can encounter, how to prevent them, and so on. She is very caring and highly professional, knowing how to strike the right balance between gentleness, caution, and firmness when handling a cat. You can tell she genuinely cares about the well-being of our furry friends, and I'm always reassured knowing Elio and Naïa are in her expert hands. The rest of the team is also always friendly, smiling, and attentive. I recommend this clinic without hesitation and thank the entire team for their professionalism!

I took my 11-month-old kitten for her first checkup. We were very warmly welcomed by Dr. Stéphanie Trubert. Despite my kitten's anxiety, Dr. Trubert took the time to reassure her. A consultation with a really nice vet, and Zelda is doing much better with the appropriate treatment. Everything is fine.

I am a client of this clinic.

In March, I called in an emergency on a Friday around 2 PM because my cat was trying to use his litter box ten times in a row, only to come out without having urinated and let out plaintive meows (even though he's usually a very quiet cat). The only available appointment was the following Monday at 5 PM. I emphasized the urgency of his condition. I was told I had to stop feeding him dry food and switch to wet food pouches, and that there was no possibility of seeing my cat in an emergency. I was given the phone number of a clinic supposedly open 24/7. I called on Saturday morning at 6 AM and actually got a switchboard, which then transferred me to a professional who finally told me that this clinic only opened at 9 AM and that I had to contact them after that time.

I ended up calling another veterinarian who told me to come in immediately because it was an emergency. Indeed, after a simple x-ray, it was discovered that my cat had a huge bladder stone.

Result: my cat could have died!

It's a shame they don't know how to handle emergencies from clients who never call without a reason.

@ your reply: you are right to justify yourself with your response below, and this without even having examined the cat!!! Very professional indeed!!
Best of luck to you too

A truly remarkable moment in veterinary medicine this afternoon at this "veterinary lab." I came for a simple blood test on my cat, just to check if her rabies vaccination had taken effect. A routine procedure I've already had done elsewhere, without any problems. Each time, I was present. But here, I was simply forbidden from accompanying my pet. Utterly absurd.

So I had to wait alone in the waiting room while my cat was taken to the basement.

Literally three minutes later, the "veterinarian" and her "assistant" returned: "It's impossible, she's struggling." And the icing on the cake: the veterinarian very seriously announced that, to successfully complete the blood test… the cat would have to be anesthetized.

Not only is this completely disproportionate—we're talking about a simple blood draw on a cat—but it's also potentially dangerous. All because the team is incapable of doing their job with even a modicum of skill and gentleness. We're talking about veterinarians who lose their composure when faced with a slightly stressed cat.

And to top it all off: the vet's surreal justification, "You know, calico cats often have a bad temper." Excuse me? Since when is coat color a clinical criterion? Is this medicine or astrology?

Once again: your job is to treat animals, not make excuses. If a simple blood test requires anesthesia at your clinic, then there's a serious competence problem. Change your methods, or change professions.

60 euros down the drain for a three-minute wait, zero care, and a stressed cat for no reason.

I came here expecting professionalism, and I got a farce.

I hesitated for a long time before leaving a negative review because I don't like the idea, but I walk past it several times a week and I remember the disappointment this practice caused. Faced with so many glowing reviews, I'd like to offer a bit of nuance. My dog ​​was treated at this clinic (formerly Family Vet) from birth (2019) until the summer of 2024. I have no complaints about the interaction between the vet and my very timid dog. Her interactions with humans are a bit hit-or-miss, but ultimately it doesn't matter; I'm there for my dog!

However, I'm very disappointed with their practices. The prices have increased dramatically in just a few years and are now significantly higher than other vets in the neighborhood (who are already expensive), even on dog food (easily a markup of 4 or 5 euros more on the same bag, or on Veggident toothpaste-based kibble, for example). Again, if my dog ​​is well cared for, why not... But what bothered me most was the lack of consideration shown to my dog. The last time we went, in July 2024, my dog ​​had just had surgery for acute kidney failure in the context of chronic kidney disease. After having my dog ​​operated on at Sevetys (2400 euros) in the 12th arrondissement three days earlier, I took her to Rue Monge on the advice of Sevetys 12 because she was very ill. They couldn't find out what was wrong with her, but 240 euros were spent on blood tests and injections, not covered as a follow-up consultation but charged in full. My dog ​​was in very poor condition, and the vet seemed worried. Finally, three days later, I rushed her to the emergency vet in Maisons-Alfort, where she was hospitalized for several days due to post-operative complications and another episode of acute kidney failure (no post-operative consultation had been offered to me at the clinic where she had her surgery, Sevetys). No one from Sevetys ever called me to find out what had happened, if my dog ​​had survived, or what the problem was. I find it rather sad that a seriously ill, young dog, who had been followed at that clinic since she was a puppy, was treated with such consideration. Furthermore, I am aware that my dog's case, which involves numerous serious illnesses, is exceptional, and that such cases should be treated in specialized facilities (which is the case here), but the diagnosis was sometimes lacking in rigor, precisely because she was young. Even though Tini is seen by specialists, I need a local vet for the minimum monthly check-ups (blood tests, urine analyses). I finally found a less expensive place that's more caring about my dog's well-being just a few streets away.
